content.title: Who has a green jacket? A complete list of Masters winners 1934 to 2025
content.text: April 6, 2026, 10:04 a.m. ETThis weekend, one golfer will be named the champion of the 90th Masters. To win a green jacket at the Augusta National is to become part of an elite club and a massive achievement in golf.Here's a comprehensive list of the various winners since 1934 including highlights like youngest and oldest champions:Masters winners by year: List of championsSeveral players have multiple green jackets in 89 tournaments. Here's a complete list of winners:2025 - Rory McIlroy2024 - Scottie Scheffler2023 - Jon Rahm2022 - Scottie Scheffler2021 - Hideki Matsuyama2020 - Dustin Johnson2019 - Tiger Woods2018 - Patrick Reed2017 - Sergio Garcia2016 - Danny Willett2015 - Jordan Spieth2014 - Bubba Watson2013 - Adam Scott2012 - Bubba Watson2011 - Charl Schwartzel2010 - Phil Mickelson2009 - Angel Cabrera2008 - Trevor Immelman2007 - Zach Johnson2006 - Phil Mickelson2005 - Tiger Woods2004 - Phil Mickelson2003 - Mike Weir2002 - Tiger Woods2001 - Tiger Woods2000 - Vijay Singh1999 - Jose Maria Olazabal1998 - Mark O'Meara1997 - Tiger Woods1996 - Nick Faldo1995 - Ben Crenshaw1994 - Jose Maria Olazabal1993 - Bernhard Langer1992 - Fred Couples1991 - Ian Woosnam1990 - Nick Faldo1989 - Nick Faldo1988 - Sandy Lyle1987 - Larry Mize1986 - Jack Nicklaus1985 - Bernhard Langer1984 - Ben Crenshaw1983 - Seve Ballesteros1982 - Craig Stadler1981 - Tom Watson1980 - Seve Ballesteros1979 - Fuzzy Zoeller1978 - Gary Player1977 - Tom Watson1976 - Ray Floyd1975 - Jack Nicklaus1974 - Gary Player1973 - Tommy Aaron1972 - Jack Nicklaus1971 - Charles Coody1970 - Billy Casper1969 - George Archer1968 - Bob Goalby1967 - Gay Brewer1966 - Jack Nicklaus1965 - Jack Nicklaus1964 - Arnold Palmer1963 - Jack Nicklaus1962 - Arnold Palmer1961 - Gary Player1960 - Arnold Palmer1959 - Art Wall Jr.1958 - Arnold Palmer1957 - Doug Ford1956 - Jack Burke Jr1955 - Cary Middlecoff1954 - Sam Snead1953 - Ben Hogan1952 - Sam Snead1951 - Ben Hogan1950 - Jimmy Demaret1949 - Sam Snead1948 - Claude Harmon1947 - Jimmy Demaret1946 - Herman Keiser1942 - Byron Nelson1941 - Craig Wood1940 - Jimmy Demaret1939 - Ralph Guldahl1938 - Henry Picard1937 - Byron Nelson1936 - Horton Smith1935 - Gene Sarazen1934 - Horton SmithNote: 1943-1945 were not held because of World War IIWho won the Masters last year?Rory McIlroy won his first Masters last year, defeating Justin Rose in a sudden-death playoff. This also marked the completion of his career Grand Slam.Who won the first Masters?Horton Smith won the first Masters in 1934 with a 4-under par, receiving a prize of $1,500 which in today's money is almost $37,000, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' inflation calculator. For comparison, Rory McIlroy walked away from the Augusta National last year with $4.2 million.How many times has Tiger Woods won the Masters?Tiger Woods has won the Masters five times including 1997, 2001, 2002, 2005, and 2009. He is not playing at this year's Masters due to a recent rollover accident in which he was cited and taken to jail for a DUI. He blew a 0.0 on a breathalyzer, but had prescription pills on him in his vehicle.Woods said he is "stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health."The Masters responded with support for the five-time champion.Who has the most Masters wins?Jack Nicklaus: 6Tiger Woods: 5Arnold Palmer: 4Jimmy Demaret, Sam Snead, Gary Player, Nick Faldo, Phil Mickelson: 3Horton Smith, Byron Nelson, Ben Hogan, Scottie Scheffler, Tom Watson, Seve Ballesteros, Bernhard Langer, Ben Crenshaw, Jose Maria Olazabal, Bubba Watson: 2Who is the youngest Masters champion?Tiger Woods still holds the record for youngest person to ever win the Masters for his victory in 1997 at 21 years old. Interestingly, his 2019 win at age 43 also makes him the second oldest Masters champion.Who is the oldest Masters champion?Jack Nicklaus still holds the record for oldest person to ever win the Masters for his victory in 1986 at 46 years old.Miguel Legoas is a Deep South Connect Team Reporter for USA Today.
